rows.source_meaning: state space (S1)-(S5), finite-dimensional
rows.mapping: identical token. K is the convex set of normalised states, not its span and not the cone A(K)^{*+}.
rows.how: read in the arXiv TeX source at this line

rows.quote: Let $K$ be a state space and let $x \in K$.
rows.source_meaning: states (points of K)
rows.mapping: bound variables; kept as x, y, z in D2-D12. In the script x is an elementary outcome (TR-TPC-09); in a classical theory outcomes are the pure states, not the states.
rows.how: read in the arXiv TeX source at this line

rows.quote: the \emph{effect algebra} over $K$ will be denoted $E(K)$
rows.source_meaning: set of affine f: K → [0,1]
rows.mapping: identical token, macro \EffAlg{K}. Equals the whole order interval [0, 1_K] only because no restriction is assumed (D12).
rows.how: read in the arXiv TeX source at this line

rows.quote: $E(K)$ is the set of all affine functions $f: K \to [0,1]$
rows.source_meaning: effects; elements of A(K)
rows.mapping: bound variables; kept as f. In quantum theory f corresponds to the operator via f_X(ρ) = Tr(ρX) (TR-PLA-13); the letter of the quantum effect operator is open (COL-F).
rows.how: read in the arXiv TeX source at this line

rows.quote: $1_K \in E(K)$ is the constant function given as $1_K(x) = 1$ for all $x \in K$.
rows.source_meaning: unit effect
rows.mapping: identical token, macro \UnitEff{K}. In quantum theory it corresponds to the identity operator.
rows.how: read in the arXiv TeX source at this line

rows.quote: Let $A(K)$ be the vector space of affine functions on $K$ and let $A(K)^+$ be the cone of positive affine functions on $K$
rows.source_meaning: affine functions on K and their positive cone
rows.mapping: identical tokens. A(K)^+ is the cone on the effect side; it must not be confused with the cone of unnormalised states A(K)^{*+}.
rows.how: read in the arXiv TeX source at this line

rows.quote: Let $A(K)^*$ denote the dual vector space to $A(K)$
rows.source_meaning: dual vector space of A(K)
rows.mapping: identical token.
rows.how: read in the arXiv TeX source at this line

rows.source_meaning: dual cone: positive functionals on A(K)
rows.mapping: identical token. K is its base, cut out by ⟨φ, 1_K⟩ = 1 (Plavala's theorem at basic_v3.tex:178-182).
rows.how: read in the arXiv TeX source at this line

rows.source_meaning: pairing, state (functional) first, effect second
rows.mapping: \pair{x}{f}; same slot order (CONV-PAIRING). Not an inner product: the two slots are in different spaces.
rows.how: read in the arXiv TeX source at this line

rows.quote: \emph{Order unit space} $(V, \leq, u)$ is an ordered vector space $(V, \leq)$ with an order unit $u \in V$
rows.source_meaning: order unit; order unit space
rows.mapping: identical token u. Plavala's V here is a generic ordered vector space; elsewhere (basic_v3.tex:218) V = aff(K) is the ambient space of K. V has no canonical symbol (COL-V).
rows.how: read in the arXiv TeX source at this line

rows.quote: \emph{Classical theory} is a theory where the state space is a simplex $S_n$, $n \in \NN$.
rows.source_meaning: simplex with n pure states
rows.mapping: S_n → Δ_n (\Simplex{n}); pure renaming, provisional (COL-S, COL-DELTA). Plavala's S(E) (basic_v3.tex:541) is a different object and has no canonical symbol.
rows.how: read in the arXiv TeX source at this line

rows.quote: We will denote the set of all channels $\Phi: K_A \to K_B$ by $\chan(K_A, K_B)$.
rows.source_meaning: set of channels
rows.mapping: identical token, macro \Chan{K_A}{K_B}.
rows.how: read in the arXiv TeX source at this line

rows.source_meaning: measurement as a channel into the simplex
rows.mapping: bound variable m inside D9 only. Globally m is the magnetic quantum number (sym.magnetic-quantum-number).
rows.how: read in the arXiv TeX source at this line

rows.quote: the corresponding function $f_X \in A(\dens(\Ha))$ is given as $f_X(\rho) = \Tr(\rho X)$
rows.source_meaning: effect-side functional of a self-adjoint operator
rows.mapping: ⟨ρ, X⟩ = tr(ρX): the GPT pairing becomes the trace pairing. Holds for finite-dimensional ℋ only (QT_v3.tex:6).
rows.how: read in the arXiv TeX source at this line

rows.source_meaning: set of density operators
rows.mapping: identical token, macro \DensOps{\Hil} (proposed). Finite-dimensional ℋ.
rows.how: read in the arXiv TeX source at this line

rows.quote: $\bound_H(\Ha)$ will denote the real vector space of self-adjoint operators
rows.source_meaning: real vector space of self-adjoint operators (finite dimension)
rows.mapping: → B(ℋ)_sa (proposed). Plavala's \mathcal{B} carries the subscript H for Hermitian; without it the symbol does not occur in his text. His \lin(\Ha) = \mathcal{L}(\mathcal{H}) is all operators.
rows.how: read in the arXiv TeX source at this line

rows.source_meaning: set of effect operators
rows.mapping: identical token, macro \EffOps{\Hil} (proposed).
rows.how: read in the arXiv TeX source at this line

rows.source_meaning: identity operator
rows.mapping: 𝟙 → 𝕀 (\Id); glyph only.
rows.how: read in the arXiv TeX source at this line

rows.source_meaning: trace
rows.mapping: Tr → tr; same unnormalised trace (CONV-TRACE).
rows.how: read in the arXiv TeX source at this line

rows.quote: the inner product of $\ket{\psi}, \ket{\varphi} \in \Ha$ is then denoted $\braket{\varphi|\psi}$ and it is linear in the second argument
rows.source_meaning: inner product, linear in the second argument
rows.mapping: same convention (CONV-INNER); Plavala's \braket takes one argument, the registry's two.
rows.how: read in the arXiv TeX source at this line

rows.quote: This assumption is in literature called the no-restriction hypothesis.
rows.source_meaning: every element of E(K) is a physical yes-no question
rows.mapping: same term; German rendering 'Hypothese der Nichteinschränkung' is the registry's.
rows.how: read in the arXiv TeX source at this line
